name: Llama.cpp Server
description: Fast local LLM inference (llama.cpp server). Pick which GGUF to load in its Model selector.

files.install-llama-cpp.ps1:
# install-llama-cpp.ps1
#
# Downloads the official prebuilt llama.cpp server binary for Windows and
# drops it under %OAIY_BIN_DIR%. Picks the right asset for the host's
# capabilities (CUDA if present, CPU/AVX2 otherwise -- heuristic via
# `nvidia-smi` lookup).
#
# Env vars supplied by OAIY Desktop:
#   OAIY_BIN_DIR     where to drop the extracted binaries
#   OAIY_MODELS_DIR  reserved for future use (model downloads)
#
# This script ships INLINE in templates/llama-cpp.json (the `files` map), so the
# whole service installs from that one .json. To pin a different llama.cpp build
# or point at a custom binary, edit that template.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
# Silence Invoke-WebRequest's progress bar — it's slow and can stall the
# download in a piped (no-console) context like the install runner.
$ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'

if (-not $env:OAIY_BIN_DIR) {
    Write-Error 'OAIY_BIN_DIR is not set; this script expects to be invoked by the OAIY app.'
    exit 1
}

$binDir = $env:OAIY_BIN_DIR
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $binDir | Out-Null

# Pinned for reproducibility; bump as needed (matches install-llama-cpp.sh).
$release = 'b9802'

# Pick CUDA build when an NVIDIA GPU + CUDA runtime appear to be present,
# else fall back to CPU. Both binaries serve the same HTTP API. The CUDA 13.3
# build targets modern archs INCLUDING Blackwell / RTX 50-series (sm_120).
$useCuda = $false
try {
    $null = Get-Command nvidia-smi -ErrorAction Stop
    & nvidia-smi | Out-Null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { $useCuda = $true }
} catch {}

if ($useCuda) {
    $assetName = "llama-$release-bin-win-cuda-13.3-x64.zip"
    Write-Host "[install-llama-cpp] NVIDIA GPU detected -- downloading CUDA 13.3 build (supports Blackwell / RTX 50-series sm_120)"
} else {
    $assetName = "llama-$release-bin-win-cpu-x64.zip"
    Write-Host "[install-llama-cpp] No CUDA detected -- downloading CPU build"
}

$url = "https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/$release/$assetName"
$zipPath = Join-Path $env:TEMP $assetName

Write-Host "[install-llama-cpp] downloading $url"
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $zipPath -UseBasicParsing

Write-Host "[install-llama-cpp] extracting to $binDir"
Expand-Archive -Path $zipPath -DestinationPath $binDir -Force
Remove-Item $zipPath -Force

if ($useCuda) {
    # The CUDA build's zip does NOT bundle the CUDA runtime DLLs (cudart/cublas);
    # they ship in a separate, non-versioned asset. Without them llama-server.exe
    # fails to launch with a missing-DLL error on hosts without a CUDA toolkit.
    $cudart = "cudart-llama-bin-win-cuda-13.3-x64.zip"
    $cudartUrl = "https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/$release/$cudart"
    $cudartZip = Join-Path $env:TEMP $cudart
    Write-Host "[install-llama-cpp] downloading CUDA runtime DLLs $cudartUrl"
    Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $cudartUrl -OutFile $cudartZip -UseBasicParsing
    Expand-Archive -Path $cudartZip -DestinationPath $binDir -Force
    Remove-Item $cudartZip -Force
}

# Verify the binary landed where the template expects.
$exe = Join-Path $binDir 'llama-server.exe'
if (-not (Test-Path $exe)) {
    Write-Error "Expected $exe after extraction but it's missing. Release layout may have changed."
    exit 2
}

Write-Host "[install-llama-cpp] done. llama-server.exe is at $exe"
Write-Host "[install-llama-cpp] Pick which GGUF to load in the service's Model selector, then start it."
files.install-llama-cpp.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# install-llama-cpp.sh
#
# Downloads the prebuilt llama.cpp server (Linux x64, CPU) and drops it under
# $OAIY_BIN_DIR. CUDA users should build from source (the prebuilt CUDA Linux
# assets aren't published for every release); the CPU build serves the same
# OpenAI-compatible HTTP API.
#
# Ships INLINE in templates/llama-cpp.json (the `files` map), so the whole
# service installs from that one .json.
#
# Env: OAIY_BIN_DIR (where to put binaries), OAIY_MODELS_DIR (reserved).

set -e

if [ -z "$OAIY_BIN_DIR" ]; then
  echo "[install-llama-cpp] OAIY_BIN_DIR not set; run via the OAIY app/server." >&2
  exit 1
fi
mkdir -p "$OAIY_BIN_DIR"

# Pinned for reproducibility; bump as needed (matches install-llama-cpp.ps1).
release="b9802"
# The Linux build is published as a gzip tarball (NOT a .zip like Windows).
asset="llama-$release-bin-ubuntu-x64.tar.gz"
url="https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/$release/$asset"

tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

echo "[install-llama-cpp] downloading $url"
curl -fL "$url" -o "$tmp/$asset"

echo "[install-llama-cpp] extracting"
mkdir -p "$tmp/x"
tar -xzf "$tmp/$asset" -C "$tmp/x"

# Linux release zips nest binaries (e.g. build/bin/); flatten into OAIY_BIN_DIR.
server="$(find "$tmp/x" -name llama-server -type f | head -1)"
if [ -z "$server" ]; then
  echo "[install-llama-cpp] llama-server not found in the release archive (layout may have changed)." >&2
  exit 3
fi
# Copy the server + any sibling shared libs it links against.
cp "$(dirname "$server")"/* "$OAIY_BIN_DIR"/ 2>/dev/null || true
cp "$server" "$OAIY_BIN_DIR/llama-server"
chmod +x "$OAIY_BIN_DIR/llama-server"

echo "[install-llama-cpp] done — $OAIY_BIN_DIR/llama-server (CPU build)."
echo "[install-llama-cpp] Pick which GGUF to load in the service's Model selector, then start it. For CUDA, build llama.cpp from source."
